1	# Route decision — the mathematical architecture of the rebuild
2	
3	*2026-07-11, Fable-5 design session. Inputs: a 5-agent survey (mathlib v4.31.0 capability
4	inventory; old-draft map; Kleiman/FGA route DAG; alternative-routes survey; operational
5	lessons). Survey reports are archived in the session scratchpad; their load-bearing
6	conclusions are restated here so this document is self-contained.*
7	
8	This document fixes the route for all 14 protected targets in
9	`AlgebraicJacobian/Challenge.lean` and the design rules every wave must follow.
10	It is the map; the blueprint is the mathematics; the Lean tree is the proof.
11	
12	## 1. The route in one paragraph
13	
14	**`Jacobian C := Pic⁰_{C/k}`**, the identity component of the scheme representing the
15	étale-sheafified relative Picard functor of `C/k` (Kleiman, *The Picard Scheme*, FGA
16	Explained ch. 5). Representability is the central mountain (Grothendieck's Thm 4.8,
17	specialized hard to a smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve over a field).
18	The Albanese universal property is proved Milne-style (*Abelian Varieties* III.6.1):
19	symmetric powers `C^(g) → J` birational, rational maps into abelian varieties extend
20	(Milne I.3.2 = I.3.1 + Lemma 3.3), rigidity makes the factorization a homomorphism,
21	uniqueness descends from `k̄` to `k`. The genus is `g(C) := dim_k H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` with
22	`H¹` the derived-functor cohomology of the Zariski site of `C` valued in `ModuleCat k`,
23	computed by a pinned 2-affine-cover Mayer–Vietoris cokernel and proved finite by the
24	two-lattice ladder over a finite map `C → ℙ¹`. Every functorial target (`functor`,
25	`baseChangeIso`, the coherences) is a uniqueness-of-representing-object corollary of a
26	single pinned `RepresentableBy` datum — never a `Classical.choice` extraction.
27	
28	Why not the alternatives (survey verdicts):
29	
30	- **Weil group-chunk construction (Sym^g + birational group law): rejected.** Its
31	  obligations (scheme quotients by finite groups, relative divisors,
32	  cohomology-and-base-change, Weil's globalization theorem, plus a descent problem for
33	  pointless curves — the challenge's `Jacobian` takes **no rational point**) meet or
34	  exceed the FGA debt, and the functorial targets would still have to be re-derived
35	  through the Pic functor afterwards (Milne III.7.6). FGA's Thm 4.8 needs no point;
36	  that is a structural advantage for this exact statement file.
37	- **Kleiman's own Albanese derivation (`rmk:Alb`): rejected** — it outsources dual
38	  abelian varieties, autoduality (`Ĵ ≅ J`, [EGK Thm 2.1], unproved in our references)
39	  and projectivity of abelian varieties. Milne III.6.1 is strictly lighter and its
40	  ingredients (Sym^g, Riemann–Roch) are shared with the `Div^d`-representability leg,
41	  so their cost is amortized.
42	
43	## 2. Ground truth about mathlib v4.31.0 (verified in the checkout, not from memory)
44	
45	**Gifts to design around** (all present):
46	
47	- Group objects: `GrpObj`, bundled `Grp C`, `Functor.mapGrp/mapGrpIdIso/mapGrpCompIso/
48	  mapGrpNatIso` — the challenge's vocabulary, complete. **`GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy`**:
49	  a representing object of a group-valued functor gets `GrpObj` for free.
50	- `AlgebraicGeometry/Group/Abelian.lean`: `isCommMonObj_of_isProper_of_geometricallyIntegral`
51	  (proper geometrically integral group scheme over a field is commutative) — the
52	  rigidity *corollary* is already a theorem.
53	- `AlgebraicGeometry/Group/Smooth.lean`: `smooth_of_grpObj` (geometrically reduced +
54	  locally finite type group scheme over a field ⇒ smooth) — kills the deformation-theory
55	  half of smoothness; what remains of `smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus` is
56	  `T₀J ≅ H¹(C,𝒪_C)` plus dimension bookkeeping.
57	- `Sites/Representability.lean` (Zariski sheaf glued from representable opens is
58	  representable, Stacks 01JJ), `subcanonical_zariskiTopology`, the étale/fppf/fpqc sites.
59	- `ZariskisMainTheorem.lean`: `IsFinite.of_isProper_of_locallyQuasiFinite` — the
60	  finite-map-to-ℙ¹ leg shrinks.
61	- Sheaf cohomology `Sheaf.H` via `Ext` + Grothendieck-abelian `HasExt`/`EnoughInjectives`
62	  + the Mayer–Vietoris LES (`Sites/SheafCohomology/`) — at `AddCommGrpCat`; the
63	  `ModuleCat k` twin is ours to build (de-risked: the old draft did it).
64	- `IsProper`/`SmoothOfRelativeDimension`/`Geometrically*` with exactly the stability
65	  instances the frozen file consumes; valuative criterion over arbitrary valuation rings;
66	  `Proj` + its properness; function fields; Dedekind/`HeightOneSpectrum` valuation stack;
67	  `RingTheory/Invariant` (`A^G`); rational maps (`Birational/RationalMap.lean` — no
68	  extension theorems though).
69	
70	**Load-bearing absences** (each is ours to build; nothing above Layer A of the DAG exists):
71	coherent cohomology of schemes (any `H^i(X,F)`, `R^i f_*`, base change, finiteness,
72	vanishing); line bundles / `Pic` of a scheme; Weil/Cartier divisors, degrees, `L(D)`;
73	Riemann–Roch / Serre duality in any form; ampleness / projectivity vocabulary / `𝒪(d)` /
74	Serre finiteness; Hilbert/Quot/Grassmannian schemes; quotients of schemes (finite groups
75	or equivalence relations); symmetric powers; relative effective divisors; rigidity;
76	rational-map extension theorems; smooth ⇒ geometrically reduced; Auslander–Buchsbaum;
77	DVR refinement of the valuative criterion; genus (zero hits in all of Mathlib).
78	
79	## 3. Definitions of record (the semantic pins)
80	
81	- **genus**: `genus C := Module.finrank k (H¹ₖ(C, 𝒪_C))` where `Hⁿₖ(C, F)` is the
82	  Ext-based cohomology of the (essentially small) Zariski site of `C` with values in
83	  `ModuleCat k`, applied to the structure sheaf viewed as a sheaf of `k`-modules.
84	  *Not* a Čech-carrier definition: the derived definition is canonical
85	  (cover-independent by construction), mathlib-idiomatic, and the MV (0,1)-slice
86	  gives the 2-cover cokernel computation as a theorem, gate-free (old draft proved
87	  this bridge end to end; we re-derive it).
88	- **Jacobian**: the representing object of the degree-0 part of the étale-sheafified
89	  relative Picard functor, carried as a **pinned `RepresentableBy` datum** (data, not
90	  `Nonempty`), from which `instGrpObj` is `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy`, `functor.map` is
91	  precomposition of represented functors, and `baseChangeIso` + coherences are
92	  uniqueness-of-representing-object arguments.
93	- **ofCurve**: the Abel–Jacobi map `t ↦ [𝒪(Γ_t − P_T)]` via graph divisors
94	  (`Div¹_{C/k} = C`), landing in `Pic⁰` because `C` is connected and `P ↦ 0`.
95	- **Albanese UP**: Milne III.6.1 over `k̄`, descended to `k` uniqueness-first
96	  (Milne 6.4-pattern). Note the challenge asks uniqueness among **plain** `Over`-morphisms;
97	  rigidity converts any competitor into a homomorphism (it is pointed:
98	  `η ≫ g = P ≫ ofCurve P ≫ g = P ≫ f = η`), and homomorphisms agreeing on the
99	  generating curve agree.
100	
101	## 4. Proof-obligation DAG (cost-ordered waves)
102	
103	Difficulty: [R] routine, [S] substantial, [RG] research-grade-for-mathlib.
104	The four [RG] clusters are: representability (B4), Albanese (N12), properness (N5),
105	and the coherent-cohomology substrate they stand on. Everything else is [R]/[S] given
106	its predecessors.
107	
108	### Wave 1 — curve substrate + the genus lane (fully de-risked; do first)
109	1. `Curve/Basic` [R–S]: standing consequences of the hypothesis bundle — integral,
110	   quasi-compact, separated; `Γ(C,𝒪_C) ≅ k` (via mathlib's
111	   `isIso_pushoutSection_of_isQuasiSeparated_of_flat_right` + properness `isField`
112	   facts); function field; stalk dimension ≤ 1 on standard-smooth rel-dim-1 charts.
113	2. `Curve/GeometricallyReduced` [S]: **smooth ⇒ geometrically reduced** (fibers of a
114	   smooth morphism are geometrically regular). Mathlib gap under EVERY target: the
115	   frozen file says `GeometricallyIrreducible`; all the real mathematics needs
116	   `GeometricallyIntegral`. Settled here once, as an instance.
117	3. `Cohomology/*` [S]: `ModuleCat k`-valued sheaf cohomology `Hⁿₖ` (Grothendieck-abelian
118	   ⇒ `HasExt`, universe discipline fixed once); degree-1 vanishing on affines;
119	   2-affine-cover MV square + `H1Cok` cokernel carrier; the MV (0,1)-slice bridge
120	   `H¹ₖ(C,𝒪) ≃ₗ[k] H1Cok`.
121	4. `Curve/MapToP1` [S]: a nonconstant rational function spreads out to a finite
122	   `π : C → ℙ¹` (ZMT does the heavy lifting now).
123	5. `Cohomology/Finiteness` + `Genus` [S]: two-lattice ladder ⇒ `Module.Finite k H¹ₖ`;
124	   **define `genus`, discharge the first protected sorry.**
125	
126	### Wave 2 — abelian-variety generalities (parallel to late W1)
127	6. `AbelianVariety/Rigidity` [S]: Mumford Form-I rigidity over `k̄`; Milne I Cor 1.2
128	   (pointed map of AVs is a homomorphism), Cor 1.5. (Old draft proved this 908-line
129	   design; re-derive compactly, checking what `Group/Abelian.lean` already covers.)
130	7. χ-ledger / RR-lite [S]: `h⁰/h¹/χ` for line-bundle-twisted sheaves on `C` via the
131	   2-cover carrier; `χ(𝒪) = 1 − g`; degree via `deg L := χ(L) − χ(𝒪)`; Riemann
132	   inequality; principal divisors have degree 0. Feeds N2 (projectivity), Div^d, and
133	   the Albanese birationality. Serre duality is deferred until a consumer forces it
134	   (function-field route via Weil differentials if ever needed — never scheme-theoretic).
135	
136	### Wave 3 — the Picard functor and the gated spine
137	8. `Picard/LineBundles` [S]: invertible 𝒪-modules on `C ×ₖ T` *modeled by transition
138	   data on the pinned 2-cover after affine-local refinement of `T`* — no monoidal
139	   structure on sheaf categories, ever (the old draft burned ~10k lines there; its own
140	   post-mortem endorses the cocycle model).
141	9. `Picard/Functor` [S]: the rigidified/étale-sheafified `Pic_{C/k}` on affine test
142	   schemes; group-valued; degree map; `Pic⁰` sub-functor.
143	10. `Picard/Witness` [R]: the **`JacobianData C` structure** — representing object +
144	    pinned `RepresentableBy` + the instance package. Downstream waves consume
145	    `(d : JacobianData C)` as a section variable. NEVER a sorried instance
146	    (typed-sorry data poisons every consumer with `sorryAx`); NEVER `Nonempty` + choice
147	    (destroys the naturality data that `functor`/`baseChangeIso` need).
148	
149	### Wave 4 — representability [RG mountain #1]
150	11. Rigid pushforward engine (Mumford AV II.5 two-term projective replacement;
151	    `h¹`-vanishing ⇒ `q_*L` locally free of rank χ commuting with base change).
152	12. Uniform `h¹`-vanishing for large degree; `Div^d` for curves; Grassmannian/ℙ-bundle
153	    embedding; Σ-opens, equalizer, gluing over `k^s` (Stacks 01JJ); Galois descent to `k`
154	    (Speiser semilinear descent — landed cleanly in the old draft, re-derive).
155	    The old draft's judged D3 campaign decomposition (~15–20 milestones) is the map;
156	    Quot schemes / flattening / Altman–Kleiman are **off-route** (their only Kleiman
157	    consumer, `lm:qt`, is bypassed by the curve-specific `Div^d` geometry).
158	
159	### Wave 5 — the abelian-variety package for `Pic⁰` [RG mountains #2, #3]
160	13. Tangent space `T₀Pic = H¹(C,𝒪)` (dual numbers, truncated exponential) [S];
161	    smoothness via geometric reducedness at 0 + `smooth_of_grpObj` [S];
162	    `SmoothOfRelativeDimension (genus C)` assembly [S].
163	14. Properness [RG]: valuative criterion; extend a line bundle on `C_K` over `C_A`
164	    (`C_A` regular 2-dimensional ⇒ locally factorial — needs an Auslander–Buchsbaum-grade
165	    brick; budget explicitly, consider the `C^(g)`-surjection alternative if Sym^g lands
166	    first for Albanese).
167	15. Geometric irreducibility: identity-component theory (`lem:agps(3)`: `G⁰` open-closed,
168	    finite type, geometrically irreducible, formation commutes with field extension) [S].
169	    This single lemma also powers `baseChangeIso`.
170	
171	### Wave 6 — Albanese [RG mountain #2]
172	16. Sym^r C as a scheme (finite-group quotient via Γ-stable affine covers — the old
173	    draft's Galois-quotient engine design, re-derived) [S–RG]; smoothness of `C^(g)` [S];
174	    `Div^r ≅ C^(r)` [S] (shared with Wave 4!).
175	17. Rational-map extension chain: Milne I.3.1 [S], Lemma 3.3 (the four audited substeps;
176	    two were proved in the old draft) [RG], Thm 3.2 [R given both].
177	18. Milne III.6.1 assembly over `k̄` [S]; uniqueness-first Galois descent to `k` [S];
178	    `ofCurve`, `comp_ofCurve`, `exists_unique_ofCurve_comp` discharge.
179	
180	### Wave 7 — the functorial layer (cheap **by design** if Wave 3's pin is respected)
181	19. `functor` (pullback of line bundles = precomposition on represented functors;
182	    laws by uniqueness) [S-tedious]; 20. `baseChangeIso` (étale-site base-change formal
183	    identity + `(Pic⁰)_L = (Pic_L)⁰` from #15) [S]; 21. coherences + `baseChange_ofCurve`
184	    (uniqueness of isos intertwining pinned universal elements) [R–S given the pin].
185	
186	## 5. Design rules (binding for every wave; distilled from the campaign post-mortems)
187	
188	1. **Keystone funnel.** Every wave funnels to one keystone with a wide parallel base;
189	   state the *narrowest* form a consumer needs (degree-1-only vanishing beat the full
190	   Čech-to-derived comparison; i=0 affine base-change bricks beat the `R^i f_*` engine).
191	2. **Statement audit before proof.** Every pinned statement gets a semantic audit against
192	   the source before anyone proves it (the old campaign shipped three false-as-pinned
193	   statements; each cost runs). Counterexamples for rejected pins go in the blueprint.
194	3. **No sorried data, no choice-extracted witnesses.** Deep pillars are gated as Prop
195	   classes or explicit structure hypotheses; `sorry` never inhabits a def/instance.
196	4. **One pinned universal element.** `Jacobian`, `functor`, `baseChangeIso` are all
197	   defined through the same `RepresentableBy` datum; coherences become uniqueness.
198	5. **No monoidal sheaf categories; no global adele space; no general `R^i f_*` engine;
199	   no Quot schemes.** Each is a measured multi-week detour whose consumers have
200	   cheaper curve-specific substitutes.
201	6. **Files ≤ 500 lines; mathlib naming; blueprint chapter per Lean directory,
202	   1-to-1 nodes, `\leanok` only after kernel check; `\source{}` only after reading.**
203	7. **Verification bar**: `lake build <Module>` (kernel), then `lean_verify` axiom audit
204	   (`propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound` only). LSP is advisory; `lake env lean`
205	   is a false oracle (lakefile sets `maxSynthPendingDepth = 3`).
206	8. **Uniform genus.** No genus-0 fork anywhere; `J = Pic⁰` uniformly (the old draft
207	   deleted a weeks-long genus-0 lane).
208	9. **Known Lean walls + fixes** (from the ops mining, use as first resort):
209	   `Over.pullback` instance-opacity → point-level `congrArg` calc chains; defeq-blocked
210	   `𝟙` → `erw [Category.comp_id]`; functor laws by `subst`-shaped proofs; scoped
211	   `maxHeartbeats` bumps ≤ 1M (never stack past it — restructure); repeated `binop%`
212	   products hoisted into a named def; `GrpObj` is data → `letI`; `open scoped MonObj`.
213	
214	## 6. What "done" means, phase by phase
215	
216	- **Phase 1**: all 14 protected declarations sorry-free; `lake build` green;
217	  `#print axioms` on each = standard three; blueprint every node `\leanok` with sources.
218	- **Phase 2** (only after green): REVIEW.md anchors for the three headline theorems,
219	  code↔paper correspondence tightening, `ForMathlib/` extraction of the general bricks
220	  (smooth⇒geometrically reduced, identity-component theory, rigidity, MV `ModuleCat k`
221	  slice, finite-group quotients, Speiser descent are the obvious PR candidates).

1	# Wave-3 design spec — the Picard-functor lane
2	
3	*2026-07-11, Fable-5 Wave-3 design session. **Binding** for route-decision §4 items 8–10 and for
4	the interfaces Waves 4/5/7 consume. Inputs, all read in full or in the cited sections:
5	`informal/route-decision.md`, `informal/wave3-mathlib-survey.md`,
6	`informal/old-draft-picard-recon.md`, `AlgebraicJacobian/Challenge.lean` (frozen),
7	`AlgebraicJacobian/Cohomology/TwoCover.lean` (landed API), and Kleiman, *The Picard Scheme*
8	(`references/kleiman-picard-src/kleiman-picard.tex`, TeX source; reading log in §11).
9	Numbering of Kleiman items is reconstructed by counting numbered environments per section and
10	cross-checked against the known anchors (2.5 = `th:cmp`, 4.8 = `th:main`, 4.18.3 = `cor:algsch`,
11	5.1 = `lem:agps`); every citation below also gives the TeX `\label` so it is checkable
12	independently of the count.*
13	
14	Lean signatures below are **intended signatures**: binding in shape (carrier types, universes,
15	variance, what is data vs Prop), lane-owned in spelling (final names follow mathlib conventions;
16	defeq-level plumbing may adjust). Anything marked **OPEN-n** is an undecided sub-point with its
17	closing criterion in §9.
18

21	## 0. Decisions at a glance
22	
23	| # | Decision | Section |
24	|---|----------|---------|
25	| D1 | Definitional Pic = Čech H¹ of the units presheaf on the small Zariski site: **pointed covers** (one open per point), built **on mathlib's `PresheafOfGroups.H1`** fixed-family layer, refinement colimit as a sigma-type quotient, everything in `Type u`. | §2 |
26	| D2 | Group structure **multiplicative**, `CommGroup` carriers, `CommGrpCat.{u}`-valued functors. | §2.4 |
27	| D3 | Relative functor = H_T-coset quotient `Pic((C ⊗ T).left) ⧸ range(snd-pullback)` on `(Over (Spec k))ᵒᵖ`, `CommGrpCat.{u}`-valued. Never the absolute `Pic(C×T)`. | §3 |
28	| D4 | Étale sheafification = **hand-rolled one-step plus** over *presented* affine étale covers, on **affine** test schemes; extended to all of `Over (Spec k)` by the canonical limit over affine opens (dense-subsite Kan extension). One plus suffices because `relPic` is étale-separated (Kleiman 2.5(1) recast; hypothesis discharged by `ex:gc&r`). Option (iii) "representability becomes the definition" is **rejected as a definition** and retained as the Wave-4 **proof strategy**; the functor `J` represents is construction-canonical. | §4 |
29	| D5 | `JacobianData C` = structure with fields `J`, the `RepresentableBy` **datum** for the degree-0 functor, and `LocallyOfFiniteType` + `QuasiCompact` certificates. Consumed as a section variable; discharged by a Wave-4 *def* `jacobianData C`, never `Nonempty` + choice, never a sorried instance. | §5 |
30	| D6 | Degree defined over fields via the divisor/χ ledger owned by Wave 2 (interface pinned here, B4 pushforward-rank shape as the normalization `deg 𝒪(D) = finrank`); `Pic⁰` = subfunctor of classes with degree 0 at **every field-valued point** of the test scheme. | §6 |
31	| D7 | `baseChangeIso` will consume degree-invariance under field extension (χ-ledger), **not** identity-component theory; `lem:agps`(3) remains needed only for `GeometricallyIrreducible`. Deviation from route Wave-7 item 20 wording, justified in §10. | §6.3, §10 |
32	| D8 | 12 new Lean files (§7), 5 immediately parallel lanes, keystone = the `GrpObj`-derivation dry-run compile against the frozen `instGrpObj` shape. | §7 |

36	## 1. Standing conventions
37	
38	- **Universe discipline: everything at `u`.** `Scheme.{u}`, test category `Over (Spec (.of k))`
39	  with hom-types in `Type u`, all Pic carriers in `Type u`, all functors valued in
40	  `CommGrpCat.{u}`. This is forced by `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy`
41	  (`Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Cartesian/Grp.lean:35`), which couples the universe of the
42	  representing object's homs with the functor's value universe (survey "Universe landmines").
43	  `JacobianData C` itself lives in `Type (u+1)` (it contains a scheme); that is harmless.
44	- **Hypothesis bundle.** Every file uses the frozen variable block
45	  `{k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]
46	  [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]`, plus the Wave-1 derived instance
47	  `GeometricallyIntegral C.hom` (route Wave-1 item 2) whenever integrality is used.
48	- **Product language.** All products of test objects are the cartesian-monoidal product in
49	  `Over (Spec (.of k))` (`CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Cartesian/Over.lean:34`,
50	  `Over.cartesianMonoidalCategory`, chosen via `Limits.pullback`): `C ⊗ T`, projections
51	  `fst C T`, `snd C T`, whiskering `C ◁ g`. This is the vocabulary of the frozen file
52	  (`𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k)))`, `η[·]`, `Functor.LaxMonoidal.ε`). Descents to `Scheme`-level
53	  pullbacks (`(C ⊗ T).left`) happen only inside cocycle constructions, with the bridge lemmas
54	  confined to `Picard/RelFunctor.lean`. Known wall: `Over.pullback` instance opacity — use the
55	  route rule 9 fixes (point-level `congrArg` calc chains, `erw [Category.comp_id]`).
56	- **Verification bar** (route rule 7): `lake build <Module>` kernel check, then `lean_verify`
57	  axiom audit (`propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound` only) on each keystone. LSP advisory only.
58	- Category names verified in the v4.31 checkout: bundled concrete categories are `GrpCat`,
59	  `CommGrpCat`, `CommMonCat` (e.g. `CommMonCat.units : CommMonCat.{u} ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u}`,
60	  `Mathlib/Algebra/Category/Grp/Adjunctions.lean:202`); bundled group *objects* are
61	  `CategoryTheory.Grp C` (`Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Grp.lean:82`), the challenge's
62	  `Grp (Over (Spec (.of k)))`.

65	
66	## 2. (A) The definitional Pic carrier
67	
68	**Semantic pin.** For any scheme `X`, the Picard group *of record* is the Čech cohomology
69	`Ȟ¹(X, 𝒪_X^*)` on the small Zariski site: covers by opens, unit-valued 1-cocycles modulo
70	coboundaries, colimit over refinement. This is recon lesson 1 verbatim, and it is Kleiman's own
71	remark `rk:coh` (§2.11): "for any ringed space `R`, there is a natural isomorphism

82	### 2.1 Index discipline: pointed covers, arbitrary opens
83	
84	```lean
85	/-- A pointed open cover of a scheme: one open per point, containing it. -/
86	structure Scheme.PointedCover (X : Scheme.{u}) : Type u where
87	  opens : X → X.Opens
88	  mem_opens : ∀ x, x ∈ opens x
89	```
90	
91	with the refinement preorder `𝒱 ≤ 𝒰 ↔ ∀ x, 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒰.opens x`.
92	
93	Decision rationale (each alternative was weighed):
94	
95	- **Not finite covers, not affine covers, not `Set X.Opens`.** Pointed covers give:
96	  (a) *smallness for free* — the index type is the fixed carrier `X : Type u`, so the sigma type
97	  in §2.3 stays in `Type u`; (b) *canonical refinement maps* — a refinement `𝒱 ≤ 𝒰` refines
98	  **indexwise** (`𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒰.opens x`), so the cocycle-restriction map needs no choice of a
99	  reindexing function and no "independence of the refinement map" lemma at the carrier level;
100	  (c) *directedness by pointwise `⊓`* (`(𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱).opens x := 𝒰.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x`), so the
101	  refinement colimit is filtered; (d) *clean pullback* — for `f : X ⟶ Y` the pulled-back cover is
102	  `x ↦ f ⁻¹ᵁ (𝒰.opens (f x))`, again pointed, again indexed by the carrier. Affineness
103	  constraints would break (d) (preimages of affines are not affine); `Set`-indexing breaks (b)
104	  (pullback collapses indices).
105	- Affine or finite covers re-enter as *cofinality lemmas*, not as carrier structure: every
106	  pointed cover is refined by a pointed affine cover (`x ↦` an affine open neighbourhood inside
107	  `𝒰.opens x`; the choice lives inside a `Prop`, so no data escapes). This is where the
108	  2-cover computations of the χ-ledger and the T₀ engine plug in.

110	### 2.2 The cocycle layer: build on `PresheafOfGroups.H1`
111	
112	**Decision: build on mathlib's fixed-family layer**, not hand-rolled. Instantiation:
113	
114	```lean
115	/-- The units presheaf of a scheme, on its small Zariski site. -/
116	def Scheme.unitsPresheaf (X : Scheme.{u}) : (X.Opens)ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u} :=
117	  X.presheaf ⋙ forget₂ CommRingCat CommMonCat ⋙ CommMonCat.units
118	-- (OPEN-4: if the `forget₂ CommRingCat CommMonCat` path is absent in v4.31, a ~20-line
119	-- bespoke functor replaces the composition; the statement shape is unchanged.)
120	
121	abbrev Scheme.unitsCocycle (X : Scheme.{u}) (𝒰 : X.PointedCover) :=
122	  PresheafOfGroups.OneCocycle (X.unitsPresheaf ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) 𝒰.opens
123	```
124	
125	Here the site category is the poset `X.Opens`, the family is `𝒰.opens : X → X.Opens`, and
126	mathlib's `OneCochain/OneCocycle/OneCohomologyRelation/IsCohomologous/H1` + `One (H1 G U)`
127	(`Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/NonabelianCohomology/H1.lean:58–197`) come for free. On a poset
128	with infima, the `ev (i j) (a : T ⟶ U i) (b : T ⟶ U j)`-style cochain is *equivalent* to the
129	classical pair data `g x y ∈ 𝒪ˣ(𝒰x ⊓ 𝒰y)` with the cocycle condition on triple infima: homs
130	are subsingletons, so `ev` is determined by its value at `T = 𝒰x ⊓ 𝒰y` via `ev_precomp`, and
131	`ev_trans` at the triple infimum is the classical condition. **Binding ergonomic requirement**:
132	`Picard/CechH1.lean` must provide the two-way bridge so lane agents never touch `ev` directly:
133	
134	```lean
135	/-- Build a 1-cocycle over a poset with binary infima from classical pair data. -/
136	def PresheafOfGroups.OneCocycle.ofPairs
137	    (g : ∀ x y, G.obj (op (𝒰.opens x ⊓ 𝒰.opens y)))
138	    (hg : ∀ x y z, /- restrictions to the triple infimum satisfy g x y · g y z = g x z -/) :
139	    OneCocycle G 𝒰.opens
140	lemma ev_inf (γ : OneCocycle G 𝒰.opens) (x y) : γ.ev x y ⋯ = ⋯   -- extraction at the infimum
141	```
142	
143	Additions ours to make (all in `Picard/CechH1.lean`, stated generically over any `Cᵒᵖ ⥤
144	CommGrpCat.{w}` — a mathlib-PR candidate, their file's TODO list asks for exactly this):
145	
146	- `Mul/Inv/CommGroup (OneCocycle Gc U)` when the presheaf is commutative-group-valued (the
147	  product of cocycles satisfies `ev_trans` only using commutativity), and the descended
148	  `CommGroup (H1 Gc U)` via `Quot.map₂` (compatibility of `IsCohomologous` with products again
149	  uses commutativity).
150	- Restriction along an indexwise refinement `res : H1 G 𝒰 →* H1 G 𝒱` for `𝒱 ≤ 𝒰`
151	  (on cocycles: restrict values along the inclusions; strictly functorial:
152	  `res_res : res h₂ ∘ res h₁ = res (h₁.trans h₂)` holds on the nose at cochain level).

154	### 2.3 The refinement colimit
155	
156	```lean
157	/-- The definitional Picard group: Čech H¹ of the units presheaf, colimit over pointed covers. -/
158	def Scheme.CechPic (X : Scheme.{u}) : Type u :=
159	  Quot (fun p q : (Σ 𝒰 : X.PointedCover, PresheafOfGroups.H1 ⋯ 𝒰.opens) =>
160	    ∃ 𝒲, ∃ (h₁ : 𝒲 ≤ p.1) (h₂ : 𝒲 ≤ q.1), res h₁ p.2 = res h₂ q.2)
161	```
162	
163	- The relation is an equivalence *because the poset is directed* (common refinement by pointwise
164	  `⊓`) and `res` strictly composes; the standard filtered-colimit argument is elementary and
165	  choice-free.
166	- Universe accounting: `X.PointedCover : Type u`, each `H1 … : Type u` (index `X : Type u`,
167	  values in `Type u`), the sigma is `Type u`, the quotient is `Type u`. **No `ULift` anywhere.**
168	- `CommGroup (X.CechPic)`: multiplication of classes represented on a common refinement;
169	  well-definedness from §2.2's `CommGroup (H1 …)` + `res` being a group hom.
170	- Constructor/eliminator API: `CechPic.mk (𝒰) (γ : OneCocycle …) : X.CechPic`,
171	  `CechPic.ind`, `CechPic.mk_eq_mk_iff_of_refines`, and the "sanity gate"
172	  `CechPic (Spec (.of K)) ≃* PUnit`-style triviality for fields (one-point space, one cover,
173	  `ev_refl` kills every cocycle) — this is Lane 1's cheap end-to-end test.
174	
175	### 2.4 Group structure: multiplicative, `CommGrpCat`-valued
176	
177	**Decision: multiplicative.** Justification (each item load-bearing):
178	
179	1. The cocycle values are *units of rings*; their native structure is multiplicative, and
180	   `tensor product of line bundles = pointwise multiplication of transition units`,
181	   `dual = pointwise inverse` — recon lesson 1's entire point. An additive carrier would
182	   re-introduce a translation layer at exactly the spot the old draft burned.
183	2. `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` takes `F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ GrpCat.{w}` — multiplicative — and
184	   `forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat` is the canonical bridge. The old draft's
185	   `AddCommGrpCat.{u+1}` choice cost both a universe bump and an additive/multiplicative
186	   mismatch at the representability gate.
187	3. Mathlib's `PresheafOfGroups.H1` layer (§2.2) is multiplicative.
188	
189	The `ℤ`-valued *degree* (§6) is additive; the interface between the multiplicative Pic and the
190	additive degree is a single `→ ℤ` map with `deg (a * b) = deg a + deg b` — pinned as such, no
191	`Multiplicative ℤ` gymnastics in consumer-facing statements.
192	
193	### 2.5 Functoriality: pullback of cocycles
194	
195	```lean
196	def Scheme.CechPic.map {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Y.CechPic →* X.CechPic
197	theorem Scheme.CechPic.map_id (X) : CechPic.map (𝟙 X) = MonoidHom.id _
198	theorem Scheme.CechPic.map_comp (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) :
199	    CechPic.map (f ≫ g) = (CechPic.map f).comp (CechPic.map g)
200	```
201	
202	On representatives: pull the cover back pointwise through `f.base` (`x ↦ f ⁻¹ᵁ 𝒰.opens (f x)`),
203	pull the units back through `f.app`, restrict. `map_comp` compares the covers
204	`(f ≫ g) ⁻¹ᵁ 𝒰 (g (f x))` and `f ⁻¹ᵁ (g ⁻¹ᵁ 𝒰 (g (f x)))` — equal opens
205	(`Scheme.preimage_comp`), with the value comparison through `Scheme.Hom.app_comp`; if defeq
206	friction appears, prove it through the refinement relation (both sides restrict to a common
207	refinement) rather than `eqToHom` surgery.

209	### 2.6 Divisor classes as cocycles: the `𝒪(D)` constructor
210	
211	Three constructors, in dependency order. Sign convention (route §3, audited in §8):
212	a local-equation system `(fᵢ)` for an effective `D` produces the class of `𝒪(D)` with
213	transition units `g x y = f x / f y` on overlaps (trivialization of `𝒪(D)` on `𝒰x` by
214	multiplication by `f x`).
215	
216	**(a) Local-equation data → class** (`Picard/DivisorClass.lean`):
217	
218	```lean
219	/-- Local equations for an effective Cartier divisor, adapted to a pointed cover. -/
220	structure Scheme.LocalEquations (X : Scheme.{u}) : Type u where
221	  cover : X.PointedCover
222	  eqn : ∀ x, Γ(X, cover.opens x)
223	  regular : ∀ x, /- eqn x is a nonzerodivisor in every stalk over cover.opens x -/
224	  ratio_isUnit : ∀ x y, IsUnit (/- (eqn x)/(eqn y) as a section on the overlap, i.e.
225	      ∃ u : unit on 𝒰x ⊓ 𝒰y, (eqn x)|∩ = u * (eqn y)|∩ -/)
226	
227	def Scheme.LocalEquations.picClass (d : X.LocalEquations) : X.CechPic
228	  -- the class of the cocycle (x,y) ↦ the unit u x y with (eqn x)|∩ = u x y • (eqn y)|∩
229	```
230	
231	with: uniqueness of `u x y` (regularity makes the ratio unit unique — this is why `regular` is
232	part of the data), the cocycle identity for `u` (from associativity of the ratios),
233	*independence*: two `LocalEquations` cutting out the same closed subscheme (or related by
234	unitwise rescaling) have equal `picClass`; *multiplicativity*: pointwise product of equations ↦
235	product of classes; *pullback compatibility*: for `f : X' ⟶ X` such that the pulled-back
236	equations are still regular (guaranteed in the relative situation below),
237	`(d.pullback f).picClass = CechPic.map f d.picClass`.
238	
239	**(b) The two geometric instances** (`Picard/GraphDivisor.lean`):
240	
241	- *Point divisor.* For a `k`-point `P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C`, the image of `P` is an
242	  effective Cartier divisor on `C.left`: the local ring at the image point is a DVR
243	  (`Curve/StalksDVR.lean`, Wave 1), so a uniformizer spreads to a local equation, and away from
244	  the point the equation `1` works. Output: `pointDivisor P : C.left.LocalEquations` (cover:
245	  a distinguished pointed cover; the choice of uniformizer is data *inside* the construction,
246	  with `picClass`-level independence proven — see the choice-discipline note in §4.4).
247	- *Graph divisor.* The diagonal `Δ ⊂ (C ⊗ C).left` is a relative effective divisor over the
248	  **second** factor: `pr₂|Δ` is an isomorphism onto the base, in particular finite flat of rank
249	  1, and smoothness of `C/k` of relative dimension 1 makes the conormal module invertible, so
250	  the ideal of `Δ` is locally one regular equation. Deliverable:
251	
252	  ```lean
253	  def graphLocalEquations (t : T ⟶ C /- in Over (Spec k) -/) :
254	      ((C ⊗ T).left).LocalEquations   -- local equations for Γ_t := (C ◁ t)-pullback of Δ ⋯
255	  theorem graphLocalEquations_base_change ⋯  -- Γ_{t ∘ g} equations = pullback of Γ_t equations
256	  ```
257	
258	  The base-change stability is *by construction*: `Γ_t` is the pullback of the universal `Δ`
259	  along `C ◁ (t ≫ ⋯)`, and (a)'s pullback compatibility applies because `Δ` is a *relative*
260	  divisor over the test factor (fibers never contain a component of `C`), so regularity
261	  survives every base change. Rank certificate: `𝒪_{Γ_t} ≅ 𝒪_T` as `T`-algebras, so the
262	  finite-flat rank of `Γ_t → T` is 1 — the input for the degree of `abelElement` (§6).
263	  This mathematics is Kleiman `ex:DivC` (§3.8: `X₀ = Div¹_{X/S}` for the smooth locus) and
264	  `rmk:Jac` (§5.26: "Given `t : T → X`, its graph subscheme `Γ_t ⊂ X × T` is a relative
265	  effective divisor"); both read.
266	
267	**(c) The meromorphic bridge** (`Picard/MeromorphicTrivialization.lean`; needed by the degree,
268	see §6.1): for `X` *integral*, every `CechPic` class is a divisor class. Cocycle proof shape:
269	every nonempty open contains the generic point; fix a base index `x₀` and localize the cocycle
270	values `g x x₀` into the function field; these are meromorphic local equations for a Cartier
271	divisor whose class is the given one. (Classical statement: Kleiman quotes it in the proof of
272	`th:qpp&p` (§5.4): "Since `X × T` is integral, there is a divisor `D` such that `𝒪(D) = 𝓛`
273	by [Hartshorne, Ex. II 6.15]".) This file also pins `divisorClass` for *differences*
274	`D₁ − D₂` of effective data as `picClass D₁ * (picClass D₂)⁻¹`.

278	## 3. (B) The relative functor
279	
280	Recon lesson 3 is binding: the **certified false-axiom trap** (inbox I-0061) is wiring anything
281	to the absolute `Pic(C ×ₖ T)`; the honest functor is the H_T-coset quotient — Kleiman
282	`df:Pfs` (§2.2): "`Pic_{X/S}(T) := Pic(X_T)/Pic(T)`". Kleiman's `df:aPf` discussion (§2.1,
283	read) is the semantic audit anchor for *why* the absolute functor "is never representable".
284	
285	```lean
286	variable (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
287	
288	/-- The relative Picard group of `C/k` at a test object `T`: line-bundle classes on `C ⊗ T`
289	modulo classes pulled back from `T`. -/
290	def relPic (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Type u :=
291	  (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic ⧸ (Scheme.CechPic.map (CartesianMonoidalCategory.snd C T).left).range
292	-- CommGroup instance: QuotientGroup on the CommGroup of §2.3.
293	
294	/-- The relative Picard functor. -/
295	def relPicFunctor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u}
296	```
297	
298	- **Exact quotient relation**: `[L] = [L']` in `relPic T` iff
299	  `L * L'⁻¹ ∈ (CechPic.map (snd C T).left).range` — i.e. iff `L ≅ L' ⊗ pr_T^* N` for some class
300	  `N` on `T`, which in the cocycle model is literally a range condition; no `Nonempty (≅)`
301	  propositions anywhere.
302	- **Evaluation and restriction.** For `g : T' ⟶ T` in `Over (Spec (.of k))`, the map
303	  `relPicFunctor.map g.op` is descent of `CechPic.map ((C ◁ g).left)` to the quotients;
304	  well-defined by the monoidal naturality `(C ◁ g) ≫ snd C T = snd C T' ≫ g`. Functor laws
305	  from `CechPic.map_id/map_comp` plus `QuotientGroup.map` functoriality.
306	- **Universe target**: `CommGrpCat.{u}`, per §1. The functor category
307	  `(Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u}` is legitimate (`Over (Spec k) : Type (u+1)` with
308	  `Type u` homs, `CommGrpCat.{u} : Type (u+1)` with `Type u` homs).
309	- Also provided here (consumed by §4 and Wave 7): naturality in the curve,
310	  `relPicMapCurve (g : C' ⟶ C) : relPicFunctor C ⟶ relPicFunctor C'` (pullback along
311	  `g ▷ T`), strictly functorial in `g`; and the statement of the **base-field shuffle**: for
312	  `L/k` and `T' : Over (Spec (.of L))`, a canonical iso
313	  `relPic (C_L) T' ≃* relPic C ((Over.map (Spec.map _)).obj T')` induced by the scheme
314	  isomorphism `(C_L ⊗_L T').left ≅ (C ⊗_k T'ₖ).left` (`pullbackAssoc`-type; the survey's

355	### 4.2 The three options, weighed
356	
357	**(i) Hand-rolled plus-construction.** Define
358	`PicEt(T) := colim_{étale covers T'→T} ker(relPic T' ⇉ relPic (T' ×_T T'))` (equalizer form —
359	the plus needs no triple-overlap condition). One plus yields a sheaf iff the input presheaf is
360	separated; `relPic` **is** étale- (even fppf-) separated by Kleiman 2.5(1), whose hypothesis
361	holds by `ex:gc&r`. Cost: the separatedness proof (a genuine descent argument, §4.4), cover
362	smallness/indexing, colimit plumbing. Benefit: construction-canonical, evaluates concretely,
363	`relPic → PicEt` is a unit map usable everywhere, and over test schemes where a section exists
364	the unit is bijective *as a theorem* (2.5(2) recast) — exactly what Wave 4 needs over `k'`.
365	
366	**(ii) Define `PicEt` only via 2.5-comparison where sections exist + descent data elsewhere.**
367	Rejected. A piecewise definition is either non-canonical (it depends on which case a test
368	scheme falls into, and for `baseChangeIso` the case-split differs between `C/k` and `C_L/L`)
369	or secretly equal to (i) with the plus spelled out by hand. Every interface (group law, degree,
370	functoriality in `C`, base-field shuffle) would need case-coherence lemmas. The *content* of
371	(ii) — the comparison bijections — survives as the pair of theorems (C1), (C2) in §4.4.
372	
373	**(iii) Representability over `k'` + Galois descent, with `PicEt := the functor J represents`.**
374	Rejected **as a definition**, retained **as the Wave-4 proof strategy**. The blocker is
375	exactly the one the route anticipates: `baseChangeIso` must compare `(J_C)_L` with `J_{C_L}`,
376	and both must be recognized as representing *the same construction-canonical functor* over `L`.
377	If `PicEt_k` is defined as `Hom(−, J)`, the `RepresentableBy` datum is a tautology carrying no
378	information, and the comparison of `(J_C)_L` with `J_{C_L}` has no common third functor to
379	factor through — one would have to smuggle the construction back in, per-instance, at every
380	coherence. **Resolution (binding):** the functor is defined by construction (option (i)); the
381	`k'`-plus-descent argument is how Wave 4 *produces* the `RepresentableBy` datum; after Wave 4,
382	nothing downstream ever unfolds `J`, only the datum.

384	### 4.3 The decision, in two layers
385	
386	**Layer 1 — affine tests, presented covers** (`Picard/EtaleCovers.lean`, `Picard/PicEtAff.lean`).
387	
388	For `T` with `T.left` affine (`A := Γ(T.left, ⊤)`), an étale cover index is a *presentation*:
389	
390	```lean
391	/-- A presented affine étale cover of `Spec A`: a chosen finite presentation of an étale,
392	faithfully flat `A`-algebra. -/
393	structure EtCover (A : CommRingCat.{u}) : Type u where
394	  n m : ℕ
395	  relations : Fin m → MvPolynomial (Fin n) A
396	  -- carrier B := (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A) ⧸ (span of relations)
397	  etale : Algebra.Etale A B
398	  surjective : /- Spec B → Spec A surjective (with étale + fp this gives faithful flatness) -/
399	```

1	# χ-ledger lane — pre-design ground truth (run 0025, session 0002)
2	
3	*Scouting notes for Wave-2 item 7 (`RiemannRoch/Degree.lean`, interface (E-i)–(E-iv) pinned in
4	`wave3-picard-design.md` §6.1). Not yet a binding design; recorded so the eventual designer does
5	not re-derive the codebase facts below.*
6	
7	## Ground truth (verified in the tree, 2026-07-11)
8	
9	- `Sheaf.HModule' F U n` (`Cohomology/OverOpen.lean:268`) is `Abelian.Ext (freeModuleSheaf J R U) F n`
10	  — Ext **on the whole site** from the free sheaf on `U`. It is NOT slice cohomology of `U`
11	  by definition.
12	- The landed affine vanishing `IsAffineOpen.subsingleton_moduleKSheaf_hModule'_one`
13	  (`Cohomology/AffineVanishing.lean:309`) is proved **for the structure sheaf specifically**
14	  (Serre cobounding through `cokernel_app_surjective`, which manipulates `Γ`-sections of
15	  `moduleKSheaf` over basic opens). There is no general "vanishing for any sheaf iso to 𝒪 on
16	  the affine" statement in the tree.
17	- Consequence: §6.1's remark that for a 2-cover twisted sheaf `F_g` the instances
18	  `Subsingleton (HModule' F_g Vᵢ 1)` "transport along `F_g|Vᵢ ≅ 𝒪|Vᵢ`" is NOT a rewrite;
19	  a restricted iso does not act on whole-site Ext. Three honest options:
20	  1. **Slice comparison lemma** (mathlib-PR grade, reusable): `Ext^n_{Sh(X)}(j_! A, F) ≃
21	     Ext^n_{Sh(U)}(A, F|_U)` for the open embedding `j : U ↪ X` (exact `j_!`, restriction
22	     preserving injectives). Then restricted isos transport vanishing. Clean, one-time cost.
23	  2. **Re-run Serre cobounding for `F_g`**: generalize `cokernel_app_surjective` from
24	     `moduleKSheaf` to any `F` that is "invertible-glued" on the affine — inspect whether the
25	     proof only touches sections over opens `⊆ U` (if so, the restricted iso rewrites it).
26	  3. **Avoid sheaf-level twists in the χ-ledger entirely** (divisor-first, recommended below).
27	- `Scheme.twoCoverH1LinearEquiv` (`TwoCover.lean:94`) is already general-coefficients: any
28	  `F : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) (ModuleCat k)` + the two Subsingleton instances.
29	- Mathlib's `Abelian.Ext` provides the covariant LES in the second argument (SES of sheaves ⇒
30	  LES of `HModule'`), so skyscraper dévissage is available without new machinery.
31	
32	## Recommended shape (to be confirmed by the χ-design session)
33	
34	Divisor-first, mirroring the classical curve theory and the (E-i) normalization:
35	
36	- Realize `𝒪(D)` for an effective divisor `D` on the curve as the **subsheaf of the constant
37	  function-field sheaf** `K_C` cut by stalkwise order conditions (DVR stalks are landed:
38	  `Curve/StalksDVR.lean`), NOT as a cocycle twist. `𝒪 = 𝒪(0) ⊆ 𝒪(D)` with quotient a finite
39	  skyscraper of `k`-dimension `deg D` (local colengths; finite flat rank of `𝒪_D` gives (E-i)).
40	- `h⁰/h¹/χ` of these subsheaves via whole-site `HModule` + the Ext LES on
41	  `0 → 𝒪(D′) → 𝒪(D) → (skyscraper) → 0`; finiteness inherited from the landed
42	  `Module.Finite k H¹(C,𝒪)` by dévissage; `χ(𝒪(D)) = χ(𝒪) + deg D` by additivity. `χ(𝒪) = 1 − g`
43	  from `Γ(C,𝒪)=k` + the genus definition.
44	- (E-ii) hom property + well-definedness on classes: through L2's meromorphic bridge (every
45	  class is a divisor-class difference) + "principal divisors have degree 0" (order-sum of a
46	  rational function vanishes — the one genuinely new arithmetic input; Weil repartition /
47	  two-chart argument over `ℙ¹` via the landed finite `π : C → ℙ¹` is the candidate route).
48	- (E-iv) field-extension invariance: via `Cohomology/SectionsBaseChange.lean` (lane L3, in
49	  flight this session) + flat `⊗[k] K` exactness on the two-term complexes.
50	- The cocycle ↔ divisor interface stays in L2 (`DivisorClass.lean`/`MeromorphicTrivialization.lean`);
51	  the χ-ledger never needs `Subsingleton (HModule' F_g Vᵢ 1)` on this route — option 3 above,
52	  and the §6.1 coordination note to Wave 2 becomes moot.

14	`CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H'` (which is `AddCommGrpCat`-valued) at `ModuleCat R`, so that the
15	Mayer–Vietoris (0,1)-slice can be run `R`-linearly
16	(`AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.MayerVietoris`).

19	
20	* `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.freeModuleSheaf J R U` — the free sheaf of `R`-modules on `U`.
21	* `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.freeModuleSheafMap J R i` — functoriality in `U`.
22	* `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.freeModuleSheafHomEquiv` — the `R`-linear "universal property of
23	  sections": `(freeModuleSheaf J R U ⟶ F) ≃ₗ[R] F(U)`, with naturality in `F`
24	  (`freeModuleSheafHomEquiv_comp`) and in `U` (`freeModuleSheafHomEquiv_map`).
25	* `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.HModule' F U n` — `Ext^n(R[U], F)`, a `Type u` with a `Module R`
26	  structure.

30	  `Sheaf.HModule.linearEquivHModule' : HModule F n ≃ₗ[R] HModule' F T n`: cohomology of
31	  the site (`Sheaf.HModule`) is cohomology of a terminal object.

35	Morphisms out of `freeModuleSheaf J R U` are computed from the sheafification universal
36	property (`sheafifyLift`) against the explicit presheaf morphism `freeModuleSheafDesc`

9	/-!
10	# Degree-one cohomology vanishing on affine opens
11	
12	The keystone of the genus lane: for a scheme `X` over `Spec k` and an affine open
13	`U ≤ X`, the structure sheaf, viewed as a sheaf of `k`-modules on the small Zariski site,
14	has vanishing degree-one cohomology of `U`:
15	`Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule' (X.moduleKSheaf k) U 1)`
16	(`AlgebraicGeometry.IsAffineOpen.subsingleton_moduleKSheaf_hModule'_one`), and for `X`
17	itself affine, vanishing degree-one cohomology of the site:
18	`Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf k) 1)`
19	(`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.subsingleton_moduleKSheaf_hModule_one`).
20	
21	## Proof architecture
22	
23	`H¹'(U) = Ext¹(k[U], 𝒪ₖ)` and `H¹ = Ext¹(k_X, 𝒪ₖ)` in the Grothendieck abelian category
24	of sheaves of `k`-modules, so it suffices to have
25	(`Abelian.Ext.subsingleton_one_of_injective_of_surjective`, proved here for any abelian
26	category with `HasExt`):
27	
28	* a monomorphism `ι : 𝒪ₖ ⟶ G` with `G` injective — supplied by `Injective.under`
29	  (the category is Grothendieck abelian, hence has enough injectives); and
30	* surjectivity of `Hom(L, G) ⟶ Hom(L, cokernel ι)` for `L = k[U]` resp. `L = k_X` —
31	  since morphisms out of `k[U]` (resp. `k_X`) compute sections over `U` (resp. `⊤`),
32	  this is surjectivity of `G(U) ⟶ (cokernel ι)(U)` on sections over the affine open
33	  (`IsAffineOpen.cokernel_app_surjective`), which is the geometric content:
34	
35	a section `q` of `cokernel ι` over `U` lifts locally to `G` (epimorphisms of sheaves are
36	locally surjective), on a finite cover of `U` by basic opens (affine opens are
37	quasi-compact); the differences of the local lifts are a Čech 1-cocycle with values
38	in `𝒪ₖ` (kernel-exactness of sections), which on an affine open is a coboundary
39	(`IsAffineOpen.exists_cech_cobounding`, Serre's argument); correcting the local lifts by
40	the coboundary makes them glue to a lift of `q` over `U`.
41	
42	No flasque/Godement machinery and no derived-functor comparison is needed: injectivity
43	enters only through `Ext¹(L, G) = 0` for `G` injective.
44	-/

63	    (hsurj : ∀ φ : L ⟶ cokernel ι, ∃ ψ : L ⟶ I, ψ ≫ cokernel.π ι = φ) :

65	  suffices h : ∀ z : Abelian.Ext L A 1, z = 0 from ⟨fun x y ↦ (h x).trans (h y).symm⟩
66	  intro z
67	  have hS : (ShortComplex.mk ι (cokernel.π ι) (cokernel.condition ι)).ShortExact :=
68	    { exact := ShortComplex.exact_of_g_is_cokernel _ (cokernelIsCokernel ι) }

70	  obtain ⟨x₃, hx₃⟩ := covariant_sequence_exact₁ L hS z h1 (zero_add 1)
71	  obtain ⟨ψ, hψ⟩ := hsurj (homEquiv₀ x₃)
72	  have hx₃' : mk₀ (ψ ≫ cokernel.π ι) = x₃ := by
73	    rw [hψ, mk₀_homEquiv₀_apply]

78	          comp_assoc _ _ _ rfl rfl rfl
79	    _ = 0 := by rw [hS.comp_extClass]; simp

33	  small Zariski site of `X`, for a covering pair of opens.
34	* `Scheme.twoCoverH1LinearEquiv` — the general-coefficients form: for any sheaf `F` of
35	  `k`-modules with `H¹'(U₀, F)` and `H¹'(U₁, F)` subsingletons,
36	  `HModule F 1 ≃ₗ[k] F(U₀ ⊓ U₁) ⧸ range(moduleDiff)` (reusable for twisted sheaves).
37	* `TwoCover.diff k X U₀ U₁` — the difference map `Γ(U₀) × Γ(U₁) →ₗ[k] Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁)`.
38	* `TwoCover.H1Cok k X U₀ U₁` — the cokernel carrier `Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁) ⧸ range diff`.
39	* `TwoCover.delta` — the connecting map `Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁) →ₗ[k] HModule (X.moduleKSheaf k) 1`
40	  ("class of a section on the overlap").
41	* `TwoCover.h1CokEquiv : HModule (X.moduleKSheaf k) 1 ≃ₗ[k] H1Cok k X U₀ U₁`.
42	* Compatibility: `h1CokEquiv_delta` (`h1CokEquiv ∘ delta = Quotient.mk`),
43	  `delta_surjective`, `delta_diff`, `delta_resHom_left/right` and
44	  `h1Cok_mk_resHom_left/right` (classes of sections extending to `U₀` or `U₁` vanish).
45	
46	The `k`-module structure on `Γ(X, U)` is `Scheme.overModule` (restriction of scalars
47	along the structure morphism), activated as a local instance as in
48	`AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.ModuleKSheaf`.
49	-/

61	section Square
62	
63	variable (X : Scheme.{u}) (U₀ U₁ : X.Opens)
64	
65	/-- The Mayer–Vietoris square `(U₀ ⊓ U₁, U₀, U₁, ⊤)` on the small Zariski site of a
66	scheme `X`, for two opens covering `X`. -/
67	noncomputable def Scheme.twoCoverSquare (hcov : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤) :
68	    (Opens.grothendieckTopology (X : TopCat)).MayerVietorisSquare :=
69	  Opens.mayerVietorisSquare'
70	    { X₁ := U₀ ⊓ U₁
71	      X₂ := U₀
72	      X₃ := U₁
73	      X₄ := ⊤
74	      f₁₂ := homOfLE inf_le_left
75	      f₁₃ := homOfLE inf_le_right
76	      f₂₄ := homOfLE le_top
77	      f₃₄ := homOfLE le_top
78	      fac := Subsingleton.elim _ _ } hcov.symm rfl
79	
80	end Square

82	section GeneralCoefficients
83	
84	variable (k : Type u) [CommRing k] (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of k))]
85	variable (U₀ U₁ : X.Opens)
86	
87	/-- **The two-cover H¹ computation, general coefficients.** For a sheaf `F` of
88	`k`-modules on the small Zariski site of `X`, two opens with `U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤` and
89	vanishing `H¹'(U₀, F)`, `H¹'(U₁, F)`, the degree-one cohomology of the site is the
90	cokernel of the restriction-difference map `F(U₀) × F(U₁) → F(U₀ ⊓ U₁)`. -/
91	noncomputable def Scheme.twoCoverH1LinearEquiv
92	    (F : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology (X : TopCat)) (ModuleCat.{u} k))
93	    (hcov : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤)
94	    [Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule' F U₀ 1)] [Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule' F U₁ 1)] :
95	    Sheaf.HModule F 1 ≃ₗ[k]
96	      (F.obj.obj (op (U₀ ⊓ U₁)) ⧸
97	        LinearMap.range ((X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).moduleDiff F)) :=
98	  letI : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule' F (X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).X₂ 1) :=
99	    inferInstanceAs (Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule' F U₀ 1))
100	  letI : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule' F (X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).X₃ 1) :=
101	    inferInstanceAs (Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule' F U₁ 1))
102	  (Sheaf.HModule.linearEquivHModule' (isTerminalTop : IsTerminal (⊤ : X.Opens)) F 1).trans
103	    ((X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).h1LinearEquiv F).symm
104	
105	end GeneralCoefficients

107	namespace TwoCover
108	
109	variable (k : Type u) [CommRing k] (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of k))]
110	variable (U₀ U₁ : X.Opens)
111	
112	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule
113	
114	/-- The restriction-difference map `Γ(X, U₀) × Γ(X, U₁) →ₗ[k] Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁)`,
115	`(s₀, s₁) ↦ s₀|_{U₀ ⊓ U₁} - s₁|_{U₀ ⊓ U₁}` (see `TwoCover.diff_apply`), with the
116	`k`-module structures of `Scheme.overModule`. -/
117	noncomputable def diff : (Γ(X, U₀) × Γ(X, U₁)) →ₗ[k] Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁) :=
118	  ((X.moduleKSheaf k).obj.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₀)).op).hom.comp
119	      (LinearMap.fst k _ _) -
120	    ((X.moduleKSheaf k).obj.map (homOfLE (inf_le_right : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₁)).op).hom.comp
121	      (LinearMap.snd k _ _)
122	
123	lemma diff_apply (t : Γ(X, U₀) × Γ(X, U₁)) :
124	    diff k X U₀ U₁ t = X.resHom inf_le_left t.1 - X.resHom inf_le_right t.2 :=
125	  rfl
126	
127	/-- The two-cover difference map is the Mayer–Vietoris restriction-difference map of the
128	associated square. -/
129	lemma diff_eq_moduleDiff (hcov : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤) :
130	    diff k X U₀ U₁ = (X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).moduleDiff (X.moduleKSheaf k) :=
131	  rfl
132	
133	/-- **The two-cover H¹ cokernel carrier**: the cokernel of the restriction-difference
134	map, `Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁) ⧸ range (TwoCover.diff)`. For `U₀, U₁` an affine open cover this is
135	`H¹ₖ(X, 𝒪)` (see `TwoCover.h1CokEquiv`); it is a plain quotient of section modules, so
136	`Module.finrank` arguments can be run on it directly. -/
137	noncomputable abbrev H1Cok : Type u :=
138	  Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁) ⧸ LinearMap.range (diff k X U₀ U₁)
139	
140	/-- A section extending to `U₀` has vanishing class in `H1Cok`. -/
141	lemma h1Cok_mk_resHom_left (t : Γ(X, U₀)) :
142	    (Submodule.Quotient.mk (X.resHom inf_le_left t) : H1Cok k X U₀ U₁) = 0 := by
143	  rw [Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero]
144	  exact ⟨(t, 0), by rw [diff_apply]; simp⟩
145	
146	/-- A section extending to `U₁` has vanishing class in `H1Cok`. -/
147	lemma h1Cok_mk_resHom_right (t : Γ(X, U₁)) :
148	    (Submodule.Quotient.mk (X.resHom inf_le_right t) : H1Cok k X U₀ U₁) = 0 := by
149	  rw [Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero]
150	  refine ⟨(0, -t), ?_⟩
151	  rw [diff_apply]
152	  simp
153	
154	section Bridge
155	
156	variable (hcov : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤)
157	
158	/-- The two-cover connecting map: the degree-one cohomology class of a section on the
159	overlap `U₀ ⊓ U₁`, in the cohomology `Sheaf.HModule` of the small Zariski site of `X`. -/
160	noncomputable def delta :
161	    Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁) →ₗ[k] Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf k) 1 :=
162	  ((Sheaf.HModule.linearEquivHModule' (isTerminalTop : IsTerminal (⊤ : X.Opens))
163	      (X.moduleKSheaf k) 1).symm.toLinearMap).comp
164	    ((X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).moduleDelta (X.moduleKSheaf k))
165	
166	/-- The connecting class of a difference of restrictions vanishes. -/
167	lemma delta_diff (t : Γ(X, U₀) × Γ(X, U₁)) :
168	    delta k X U₀ U₁ hcov (diff k X U₀ U₁ t) = 0 := by
169	  have h : (X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).moduleDelta (X.moduleKSheaf k)
170	      (diff k X U₀ U₁ t) = 0 :=
171	    (X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).moduleDelta_moduleDiff (X.moduleKSheaf k) t
172	  rw [show delta k X U₀ U₁ hcov (diff k X U₀ U₁ t) =
173	      (Sheaf.HModule.linearEquivHModule' (isTerminalTop : IsTerminal (⊤ : X.Opens))
174	          (X.moduleKSheaf k) 1).symm
175	        ((X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).moduleDelta (X.moduleKSheaf k)
176	          (diff k X U₀ U₁ t)) from rfl, h]
177	  exact map_zero _
178	
179	/-- The connecting class of a section extending to `U₀` vanishes. -/
180	lemma delta_resHom_left (t : Γ(X, U₀)) :
181	    delta k X U₀ U₁ hcov (X.resHom inf_le_left t) = 0 := by
182	  have h : X.resHom inf_le_left t = diff k X U₀ U₁ (t, 0) := by
183	    rw [diff_apply]
184	    simp
185	  rw [h, delta_diff]
186	
187	/-- The connecting class of a section extending to `U₁` vanishes. -/
188	lemma delta_resHom_right (t : Γ(X, U₁)) :
189	    delta k X U₀ U₁ hcov (X.resHom inf_le_right t) = 0 := by
190	  have h : X.resHom inf_le_right t = -diff k X U₀ U₁ (0, t) := by
191	    rw [diff_apply]
192	    simp
193	  rw [h, map_neg, delta_diff, neg_zero]
194	
195	variable (hU₀ : IsAffineOpen U₀) (hU₁ : IsAffineOpen U₁)
196	
197	include hU₀ hU₁ in
198	/-- For an affine two-cover, the connecting map is surjective: every degree-one class
199	comes from a section on the overlap. -/
200	lemma delta_surjective : Function.Surjective (delta k X U₀ U₁ hcov) := by
201	  haveI : Subsingleton
202	      (Sheaf.HModule' (X.moduleKSheaf k) (X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).X₂ 1) :=
203	    hU₀.subsingleton_moduleKSheaf_hModule'_one k
204	  haveI : Subsingleton
205	      (Sheaf.HModule' (X.moduleKSheaf k) (X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).X₃ 1) :=
206	    hU₁.subsingleton_moduleKSheaf_hModule'_one k
207	  intro y
208	  obtain ⟨s, hs⟩ := (X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).moduleDelta_surjective (X.moduleKSheaf k)
209	    ((Sheaf.HModule.linearEquivHModule' (isTerminalTop : IsTerminal (⊤ : X.Opens))
210	      (X.moduleKSheaf k) 1) y)
211	  refine ⟨s, ?_⟩
212	  rw [show delta k X U₀ U₁ hcov s =
213	      (Sheaf.HModule.linearEquivHModule' (isTerminalTop : IsTerminal (⊤ : X.Opens))
214	          (X.moduleKSheaf k) 1).symm
215	        ((X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).moduleDelta (X.moduleKSheaf k) s) from rfl, hs,
216	    LinearEquiv.symm_apply_apply]
217	
218	/-- **The two-affine-cover H¹ cokernel bridge.** For a scheme `X` over `Spec k` and two
219	affine opens with `U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤`, the degree-one cohomology of the structure sheaf as a
220	sheaf of `k`-modules on the small Zariski site of `X` is the cokernel of the
221	restriction-difference map on sections:
222	`H¹ₖ(X, 𝒪) ≃ₗ[k] Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁) ⧸ range((s₀, s₁) ↦ s₀|∩ - s₁|∩)`.
223	The inverse sends the class of a section on the overlap to its connecting class
224	(`TwoCover.h1CokEquiv_delta`). -/
225	noncomputable def h1CokEquiv :
226	    Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf k) 1 ≃ₗ[k] H1Cok k X U₀ U₁ :=
227	  letI : Subsingleton
228	      (Sheaf.HModule' (X.moduleKSheaf k) (X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).X₂ 1) :=
229	    hU₀.subsingleton_moduleKSheaf_hModule'_one k
230	  letI : Subsingleton
231	      (Sheaf.HModule' (X.moduleKSheaf k) (X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).X₃ 1) :=
232	    hU₁.subsingleton_moduleKSheaf_hModule'_one k
233	  (Sheaf.HModule.linearEquivHModule' (isTerminalTop : IsTerminal (⊤ : X.Opens))
234	      (X.moduleKSheaf k) 1).trans
235	    ((X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).h1LinearEquiv (X.moduleKSheaf k)).symm
236	
237	/-- Compatibility of the bridge with the connecting map: the bridge sends the connecting
238	class of a section on the overlap to its class in the cokernel. -/
239	lemma h1CokEquiv_delta (s : Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁)) :
240	    h1CokEquiv k X U₀ U₁ hcov hU₀ hU₁ (delta k X U₀ U₁ hcov s) =
241	      Submodule.Quotient.mk s := by
242	  haveI : Subsingleton
243	      (Sheaf.HModule' (X.moduleKSheaf k) (X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).X₂ 1) :=
244	    hU₀.subsingleton_moduleKSheaf_hModule'_one k
245	  haveI : Subsingleton
246	      (Sheaf.HModule' (X.moduleKSheaf k) (X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).X₃ 1) :=
247	    hU₁.subsingleton_moduleKSheaf_hModule'_one k
248	  apply ((X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).h1LinearEquiv (X.moduleKSheaf k)).injective
249	  calc ((X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).h1LinearEquiv (X.moduleKSheaf k))
250	        (h1CokEquiv k X U₀ U₁ hcov hU₀ hU₁ (delta k X U₀ U₁ hcov s))
251	      = ((X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).h1LinearEquiv (X.moduleKSheaf k))
252	          (((X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).h1LinearEquiv (X.moduleKSheaf k)).symm
253	            ((Sheaf.HModule.linearEquivHModule'
254	                (isTerminalTop : IsTerminal (⊤ : X.Opens)) (X.moduleKSheaf k) 1)
255	              ((Sheaf.HModule.linearEquivHModule'
256	                  (isTerminalTop : IsTerminal (⊤ : X.Opens)) (X.moduleKSheaf k) 1).symm
257	                ((X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).moduleDelta (X.moduleKSheaf k) s)))) :=
258	        rfl
259	    _ = (X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).moduleDelta (X.moduleKSheaf k) s := by
260	        rw [LinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply, LinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply]
261	    _ = ((X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).h1LinearEquiv (X.moduleKSheaf k))
262	          (Submodule.Quotient.mk s) :=
263	        (MayerVietorisSquare.h1LinearEquiv_mk (S := X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov)
264	          (X.moduleKSheaf k) s).symm
265	
266	/-- Compatibility of the bridge with the connecting map, inverse form: the inverse
267	bridge sends the class of a section on the overlap to its connecting class. -/
268	lemma h1CokEquiv_symm_mk (s : Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁)) :
269	    (h1CokEquiv k X U₀ U₁ hcov hU₀ hU₁).symm (Submodule.Quotient.mk s) =
270	      delta k X U₀ U₁ hcov s := by
271	  apply (h1CokEquiv k X U₀ U₁ hcov hU₀ hU₁).injective
272	  rw [LinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply, h1CokEquiv_delta]
273	
274	end Bridge

10	/-!
11	# Finiteness of `H¹(X, 𝒪_X)` via a finite morphism to the projective line
12	
13	For a scheme `X` over `Spec k` equipped with a **finite** `k`-morphism `π : X ⟶ ℙ¹`, this
14	file proves that the degree-one cohomology of the structure sheaf of `X` (as a sheaf of
15	`k`-modules on the small Zariski site, `Sheaf.HModule`) is a finite `k`-module — and derives
16	the instance for the smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve of the challenge, so that
17	`genus` is the dimension of an honestly finite-dimensional vector space.
18	
19	The proof is the *two-lattice ladder* of `AlgebraicJacobian.Algebra.TwoLattice` run on the
20	Mayer–Vietoris cokernel of `AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.TwoCover`:
21	
22	* `V i := π ⁻¹ᵁ D₊(Xᵢ)` is an affine open cover of `X`
23	  (`isAffineOpen_preimage_chartOpen`, `preimage_chartOpen_sup`), so
24	  `H¹ₖ(X, 𝒪) ≃ₗ[k] Γ(V₀ ⊓ V₁) ⧸ range (res₀ - res₁)` (`TwoCover.h1CokEquiv`);
25	* `N := Γ(X, V₀ ⊓ V₁)` is a module over the Laurent polynomial ring `k[T;T⁻¹]` through
26	  `π`'s map on sections over the chart overlap and the identification
27	  `Γ(ℙ¹, D₊(X₀X₁)) ≃ k[T,T⁻¹]` (`P1.overlapSectionsEquiv`); it is module-finite because `π`
28	  is finite (`finite_app_overlap`);
29	* `Q₀, Q₁ :=` the images of `Γ(V₀), Γ(V₁)` in `N` are `k`-submodules with
30	  `range (res₀ - res₁) = Q₀ ⊔ Q₁`; `Q₀` is stable under `T` because `T` is the restriction
31	  of the chart-0 coordinate, which extends to `V₀` (symmetrically for `Q₁` and `T⁻¹`); and
32	  `V₀ ⊓ V₁` is the basic open of the pulled-back chart coordinate inside the affine `V₀`
33	  (`P1.basicOpen_awayToSection_chartCoord`), so
34	  `IsAffineOpen.isLocalization_of_eq_basicOpen` provides the surjectivity-up-to-powers
35	  hypotheses of the two-lattice lemma.
36	
37	The `ℙ¹`-side identifications live in `AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.FinitenessP1`.
38	
39	## Main declarations
40	
41	* `AlgebraicGeometry.moduleFinite_hModule_one_of_isFinite_toP1` — **the conditional
42	  finiteness theorem**: if `π : X ⟶ ℙ¹` is finite with `π ≫ P1.structureMap k = X ↘ Spec k`,
43	  then `Module.Finite k (H¹ₖ(X, 𝒪_X))`.
44	* `AlgebraicGeometry.moduleFinite_hModule_one` — the instance for the challenge curve
45	  `C` (smooth, proper, geometrically irreducible over `k`), consuming
46	  `exists_isFinite_toP1`; it is keyed on exactly the `letI : C.left.Over (Spec (.of k))`
47	  spelling used by `genus` in `AlgebraicJacobian.Challenge`.
48	
49	`FiniteDimensional k (H¹ₖ(C, 𝒪_C))` is *definitionally* the statement of the instance
50	(`FiniteDimensional` is an abbreviation for `Module.Finite`), so no separate corollary is
51	needed.
52	-/

20	  overlap (`P1.basicOpen_awayToSection_chartCoord`);
21	* the identification of the Laurent generators `T`, `T⁻¹`, and the scalars of
22	  `Γ(ℙ¹, D₊(X₀X₁)) ≃+* k[T,T⁻¹]` as restrictions of explicit sections on the two charts
23	  (`P1.overlapSectionsEquiv_symm_T`, `…_T_neg`, `…_algebraMap`).
24	-/
25	
26	set_option autoImplicit false
27	/- Scheme-theoretic unification (mixing `P1 k` with `Proj 𝒜`, `Γ(X, U)` with functor
28	applications) needs defeq checks through semireducible definitions, as in mathlib's own
29	algebraic-geometry files. -/
30	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false

32	universe u
33	
34	open CategoryTheory MvPolynomial HomogeneousLocalization TopologicalSpace

36	namespace AlgebraicGeometry

38	section OverAlgebraMap

40	/-! ### Pulling back the structure algebra map along a morphism over `Spec k` -/
41	
42	variable {k : Type u} [CommRing k]
43	
44	/-- For a morphism `π : X ⟶ Y` of schemes over `Spec k` (compatibly with the structure
45	morphisms), pulling back sections along `π` intertwines the structure algebra maps, in
46	morphism form: restricting the structure sections of `Y` from `⊤` to `U` and applying
47	`π.appLE U V e` equals the structure sections of `X` restricted from `⊤` to `V`. -/
48	lemma Scheme.Hom.appTop_map_appLE {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (.of k))]
49	    [Y.Over (Spec (.of k))] (π : X ⟶ Y) (hπ : π ≫ (Y ↘ Spec (.of k)) = X ↘ Spec (.of k))
50	    {U : Y.Opens} {V : X.Opens} (e : V ≤ π ⁻¹ᵁ U) :
51	    (Y ↘ Spec (.of k)).appTop ≫ Y.presheaf.map (homOfLE (le_top : U ≤ ⊤)).op ≫
52	        π.appLE U V e =
53	      (X ↘ Spec (.of k)).appTop ≫ X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (le_top : V ≤ ⊤)).op := by
54	  rw [Scheme.Hom.map_appLE]
55	  change (Y ↘ Spec (.of k)).appTop ≫ π.appTop ≫
56	      X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (le_top : V ≤ ⊤)).op = _
57	  rw [← Category.assoc, ← Scheme.Hom.comp_appTop, hπ]
58	
59	/-- Elementwise form of `Scheme.Hom.appTop_map_appLE`, phrased through
60	`Scheme.overAlgebraMap`: `π` pulls the structure algebra map of `Y` back to that of `X`. -/
61	lemma Scheme.Hom.appLE_overAlgebraMap {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (.of k))]
62	    [Y.Over (Spec (.of k))] (π : X ⟶ Y) (hπ : π ≫ (Y ↘ Spec (.of k)) = X ↘ Spec (.of k))
63	    {U : Y.Opens} {V : X.Opens} (e : V ≤ π ⁻¹ᵁ U) (r : k) :
64	    (π.appLE U V e).hom (Y.overAlgebraMap k U r) = X.overAlgebraMap k V r := by
65	  have h := π.appTop_map_appLE hπ e
66	  have h2 := congr((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of k)).inv ≫ $h)
67	  exact congr((CommRingCat.Hom.hom $h2) r)
68	
69	end OverAlgebraMap

71	namespace P1

73	/-! ### The chart coordinates of `ℙ¹`: structure map and basic opens -/
74	
75	variable (k : Type u) [Field k]
76	
77	/-- The standard grading of `k[X₀, X₁]`, the graded ring underlying `P1 k`. -/
78	local notation "𝒜" => homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k
79	
80	/-- The affine chart inclusions `Spec (k[X₀,X₁]_f)₀ ⟶ ℙ¹` are morphisms over `Spec k`,
81	for any homogeneous `f` of positive degree (generalizing `P1.chartι_structureMap`). -/
82	theorem awayι_structureMap {f : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k} {m : ℕ} (f_deg : f ∈ 𝒜 m)
83	    (hm : 0 < m) :
84	    Proj.awayι 𝒜 f f_deg hm ≫ structureMap k =
85	      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (Away 𝒜 f))) := by
86	  change Proj.awayι 𝒜 f f_deg hm ≫
87	      (Proj.toSpecZero 𝒜 ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (𝒜 0)))) = _
88	  rw [Proj.awayι_toSpecZero_assoc, ← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp]
89	  rfl
90	
91	/-- The inclusion of a standard basic open of `ℙ¹` factors through its affine model. -/
92	theorem basicOpen_ι_eq {f : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k} {m : ℕ} (f_deg : f ∈ 𝒜 m) (hm : 0 < m) :
93	    (Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 f).ι = Proj.basicOpenToSpec 𝒜 f ≫ Proj.awayι 𝒜 f f_deg hm := by
94	  rw [← Proj.basicOpenIsoSpec_inv_ι 𝒜 f f_deg hm, ← Proj.basicOpenIsoSpec_hom 𝒜 f f_deg hm,
95	    Iso.hom_inv_id_assoc]
96	
97	/-- The structure algebra map of `ℙ¹` restricted to a standard basic open `D₊(f)` is the
98	composite `Γ(Spec k, ⊤) ≅ k → (k[X₀,X₁]_f)₀ → Γ(ℙ¹, D₊(f))`, in morphism form. -/
99	theorem structureMap_appTop_awayToSection {f : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k} {m : ℕ}
100	    (f_deg : f ∈ 𝒜 m) (hm : 0 < m) :
101	    (structureMap k).appTop ≫
102	        (P1 k).presheaf.map (homOfLE (le_top : Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 f ≤ ⊤)).op =
103	      (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).hom ≫ CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (Away 𝒜 f)) ≫
104	        Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 f := by
105	  have h1 : (Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 f).ι ≫ structureMap k =
106	      Proj.basicOpenToSpec 𝒜 f ≫
107	        Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (Away 𝒜 f))) := by
108	    rw [basicOpen_ι_eq k f_deg hm, Category.assoc, awayι_structureMap k f_deg hm]
109	  have h2 := congrArg Scheme.Hom.appTop h1
110	  rw [Scheme.Hom.comp_appTop, Scheme.Hom.comp_appTop] at h2
111	  have h3 : (Proj.basicOpenToSpec 𝒜 f).appTop =
112	      (Scheme.ΓSpecIso _).hom ≫ Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 f ≫
113	        (Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 f).topIso.inv :=
114	    Proj.basicOpenToSpec_app_top 𝒜 f
115	  rw [h3, Scheme.ΓSpecIso_naturality_assoc] at h2
116	  have h4 : (Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 f).ι.appTop ≫ (Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 f).topIso.hom =
117	      (P1 k).presheaf.map (homOfLE (le_top : Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 f ≤ ⊤)).op := by
118	    rw [Scheme.Opens.ι_appTop, Scheme.Opens.topIso_hom, ← Functor.map_comp, ← op_comp]
119	    exact congrArg _ (congrArg Quiver.Hom.op (Subsingleton.elim _ _))
120	  have h5 := congr($h2 ≫ (Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 f).topIso.hom)
121	  rw [Category.assoc, h4] at h5
122	  simp only [Category.assoc, Iso.inv_hom_id, Category.comp_id] at h5
123	  exact h5
124	
125	/-- `g^d/f^e = Xⱼ/Xᵢ`: the mathlib localization element of the pair `(Xᵢ, Xⱼ)` is the chart
126	coordinate (generalizing `P1.isLocalizationElem_eq` to both charts). -/
127	theorem isLocalizationElem_X_eq (i j : Fin 2) :
128	    Away.isLocalizationElem (X_mem k i) (X_mem k j) = chartCoord k i j := by
129	  rw [Away.isLocalizationElem, chartCoord_eq]
130	  congr 1
131	  exact pow_one _
132	
133	/-- **The chart coordinate cuts out the overlap**: on `ℙ¹`, the scheme-level basic open of
134	the section `t = Xⱼ/Xᵢ ∈ Γ(D₊(Xᵢ))` is the chart overlap `D₊(Xᵢ) ⊓ D₊(Xⱼ)`. -/
135	theorem basicOpen_awayToSection_chartCoord (i j : Fin 2) :
136	    (P1 k).basicOpen ((Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X i)).hom (chartCoord k i j)) =
137	      chartOpen k i ⊓ chartOpen k j := by
138	  change (Proj 𝒜).basicOpen ((Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X i)).hom (chartCoord k i j)) =
139	    Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 (X i) ⊓ Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 (X j)
140	  have hpre : (Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 (X i)).ι ⁻¹ᵁ
141	        ((Proj 𝒜).basicOpen ((Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X i)).hom (chartCoord k i j))) =
142	      (Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 (X i)).ι ⁻¹ᵁ Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 (X j) := by
143	    rw [← Scheme.Opens.toSpecΓ_preimage_basicOpen]
144	    conv_rhs => rw [basicOpen_ι_eq k (X_mem k i) one_pos]
145	    change _ = Proj.basicOpenToSpec 𝒜 (X i) ⁻¹ᵁ
146	      (Proj.awayι 𝒜 (X i) (X_mem k i) one_pos ⁻¹ᵁ Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 (X j))
147	    rw [Proj.awayι_preimage_basicOpen 𝒜 (X_mem k i) one_pos (X_mem k j) one_pos,
148	      isLocalizationElem_X_eq k i j]
149	    rfl
150	  have himg := congrArg (fun W => (Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 (X i)).ι ''ᵁ W) hpre
151	  simp only [Scheme.Hom.image_preimage_eq_opensRange_inf, Scheme.Opens.opensRange_ι]
152	    at himg
153	  have hle : (Proj 𝒜).basicOpen ((Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X i)).hom (chartCoord k i j)) ≤
154	      Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 (X i) := (Proj 𝒜).basicOpen_le _
155	  calc (Proj 𝒜).basicOpen ((Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X i)).hom (chartCoord k i j))
156	      = Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 (X i) ⊓
157	          (Proj 𝒜).basicOpen ((Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X i)).hom (chartCoord k i j)) :=
158	        (inf_eq_right.mpr hle).symm
159	    _ = Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 (X i) ⊓ Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 (X j) := himg
160	
161	/-! ### The Laurent generators as restrictions from the charts -/
162	
163	/-- Under the overlap identification, `T` is the restriction to the overlap of the chart-0
164	coordinate `X₁/X₀ ∈ Γ(D₊(X₀))`. -/
165	theorem overlapSectionsEquiv_symm_T :
166	    (overlapSectionsEquiv k).symm (LaurentPolynomial.T 1) =
167	      ((P1 k).presheaf.map (homOfLE (overlap_le_left k)).op).hom
168	        ((Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X 0)).hom (chartCoord k 0 1)) := by
169	  apply (overlapSectionsEquiv k).injective
170	  rw [RingEquiv.apply_symm_apply, res_awayToSection_left, overlapSectionsEquiv_awayToSection,
171	    overlapAlgEquiv_awayToOverlapLeft, awayAlgEquiv_chartCoord k fin_zero_ne_one,
172	    Polynomial.toLaurent_X]
173	
174	/-- Under the overlap identification, `T⁻¹` is the restriction to the overlap of the
175	chart-1 coordinate `X₀/X₁ ∈ Γ(D₊(X₁))`. -/
176	theorem overlapSectionsEquiv_symm_T_neg :
177	    (overlapSectionsEquiv k).symm (LaurentPolynomial.T (-1)) =
178	      ((P1 k).presheaf.map (homOfLE (overlap_le_right k)).op).hom
179	        ((Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X 1)).hom (chartCoord k 1 0)) := by
180	  apply (overlapSectionsEquiv k).injective
181	  rw [RingEquiv.apply_symm_apply, res_awayToSection_right, overlapSectionsEquiv_awayToSection,
182	    overlapAlgEquiv_awayToOverlapRight_chartCoord]
183	
184	/-- The overlap identification matches the algebra map of the homogeneous localization
185	with that of the Laurent polynomial ring. -/
186	theorem overlapSectionsEquiv_symm_algebraMap (r : k) :
187	    (overlapSectionsEquiv k).symm (algebraMap k (LaurentPolynomial k) r) =
188	      (Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1)).hom (algebraMap k (Away 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1)) r) := by
189	  apply (overlapSectionsEquiv k).injective
190	  rw [RingEquiv.apply_symm_apply, overlapSectionsEquiv_awayToSection]
191	  exact ((overlapAlgEquiv k).commutes r).symm
192	
193	end P1
194	
195	end AlgebraicGeometry

5	import Mathlib

7	/-!
8	# Curve substrate: basic consequences of the standing hypotheses
9	
10	The Jacobian challenge (`AlgebraicJacobian.Challenge`) works with a bundle
11	`C : Over (Spec (.of k))` together with the instances `[IsProper C.hom]`,
12	`[SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]` and `[GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]`.
13	This file records the *topological and scheme-theoretic substrate* every later wave consumes,
14	as instances keyed on the `Over`-bundle:
15	
16	* `AlgebraicGeometry.irreducibleSpace_left_of_geometricallyIrreducible`:
17	  a scheme geometrically irreducible over a field is irreducible (in particular nonempty).
18	* `AlgebraicGeometry.compactSpace_left_of_quasiCompact` and
19	  `AlgebraicGeometry.quasiSeparatedSpace_left_of_quasiSeparated`:
20	  a scheme quasi-compact (resp. quasi-separated) over `Spec k` is a quasi-compact
21	  (resp. quasi-separated) topological space; both hypotheses hold for proper morphisms.
22	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isIntegral_left_of_geometricallyReduced`:
23	  a scheme geometrically reduced and geometrically irreducible over a field is integral.
24	  In particular Mathlib's function-field API (`Scheme.functionField`) applies to `C.left`.
25	
26	Geometric reducedness is taken as a *hypothesis* here: the implication
27	"smooth ⟹ geometrically reduced" is proved elsewhere in this project
28	(`AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.GeometricallyReduced`), never in this file.
29	
30	Statements are given for an arbitrary `X : Over (Spec (.of k))` with the minimal hypotheses,
31	so that they also apply to the Jacobian bundle itself in later waves.
32	-/
33	
34	set_option autoImplicit false
35	
36	universe u
37	
38	open CategoryTheory Limits
39	
40	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
41	
42	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
43	
44	section OverField
45	
46	variable (X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
47	
48	/-- A scheme geometrically irreducible over a field is irreducible.
49	In particular it is nonempty (`IrreducibleSpace.toNonempty`). -/
50	instance irreducibleSpace_left_of_geometricallyIrreducible
51	    [GeometricallyIrreducible X.hom] : IrreducibleSpace X.left :=
52	  GeometricallyIrreducible.irreducibleSpace_of_subsingleton X.hom
53	
54	/-- A scheme quasi-compact over `Spec k` (e.g. proper) is a quasi-compact topological space. -/
55	instance compactSpace_left_of_quasiCompact [QuasiCompact X.hom] : CompactSpace X.left :=
56	  QuasiCompact.compactSpace_of_compactSpace X.hom
57	
58	/-- A scheme quasi-separated over `Spec k` (e.g. proper) is a quasi-separated topological
59	space. -/
60	instance quasiSeparatedSpace_left_of_quasiSeparated [QuasiSeparated X.hom] :
61	    QuasiSeparatedSpace X.left :=
62	  quasiSeparatedSpace_of_quasiSeparated X.hom
63	
64	/-- A scheme geometrically reduced and geometrically irreducible over a field is integral.
65	
66	Geometric reducedness is a hypothesis here; for the curve bundle of the challenge it is
67	supplied by "smooth ⟹ geometrically reduced", proved elsewhere in this project. -/
68	instance isIntegral_left_of_geometricallyReduced
69	    [GeometricallyIrreducible X.hom] [GeometricallyReduced X.hom] : IsIntegral X.left :=
70	  have : GeometricallyIntegral X.hom :=
71	    GeometricallyIntegral.of_geometricallyReduced_of_geometricallyIrreducible X.hom
72	  GeometricallyIntegral.isIntegral_of_subsingleton X.hom
73	
74	end OverField
75	
76	/-!
77	## Regression checks
78	
79	The remaining standing consequences of the hypothesis bundle are already provided by Mathlib
80	instances; the `example`s below pin them down so a Mathlib bump cannot silently lose them.
81	They are stated for the exact curve bundle of `AlgebraicJacobian.Challenge`.
82	-/
83	
84	section RegressionChecks
85	
86	variable {C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))}
87	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
88	
89	-- `IsProper` unfolds into separatedness, universal closedness and finite type,
90	-- and quasi-compactness/quasi-separatedness follow.
91	example : IsSeparated C.hom := inferInstance
92	example : UniversallyClosed C.hom := inferInstance
93	example : LocallyOfFiniteType C.hom := inferInstance
94	example : QuasiCompact C.hom := inferInstance
95	example : QuasiSeparated C.hom := inferInstance
96	
97	-- Geometric irreducibility makes the structure morphism surjective and the total space
98	-- an irreducible, nonempty, quasi-compact, quasi-separated topological space.
99	example : Surjective C.hom := inferInstance
100	example : IrreducibleSpace C.left := inferInstance
101	example : Nonempty C.left := inferInstance
102	example : CompactSpace C.left := inferInstance
103	example : QuasiSeparatedSpace C.left := inferInstance
104	
105	-- With geometric reducedness (supplied by smoothness elsewhere in this project), the curve is
106	-- integral and Mathlib's function field 𝒪_{C,η} carries its field structure and algebra maps.
107	example [GeometricallyReduced C.hom] : IsIntegral C.left := inferInstance
108	noncomputable example [GeometricallyReduced C.hom] : Field C.left.functionField := inferInstance
109	noncomputable example [GeometricallyReduced C.hom] (x : C.left) :
110	    Algebra (C.left.presheaf.stalk x) C.left.functionField := inferInstance
111	
112	end RegressionChecks
